composition.liquid-glass-welcome.boundary: Optional /welcome entry; finite gesture-driven artwork; real /onboarding and /opportunities links; does not alter account onboarding state.

composition.reader-operations.boundary: One round at a time. Progress and calibration are derived from recorded assignments and scores; distribution previews a deterministic plan with conflict reasons before writing, and the commit applies only the previewed plan. Decisions remain per Work through the existing decision route.

composition.submissions-workspace.boundary: The organization's submission list. Filters live in the address and are applied on the server. Sections order rows by the next step; bulk decisions only fill undecided Works after a confirmation, and bulk letters are drafts that still pass approval. Receipt, review and decision stay separate facts.

composition.decisions-workspace.boundary: One row per Work in sections by recorded outcome (Not decided, Accepted, Waitlisted, Declined). Filters live in the address and are applied on the server; search matches the whole submission so a piece is never shown apart from its siblings. Each Work is decided in its own dialog with the consequence stated; recording a decision never sends a letter.

composition.delivery-workspace.boundary: Accepted Works only, in sections by what their delivery task needs: Overdue, Needs setup, Active, Complete. One task per accepted Work with an optional due date; completing it in Missa proves no payment, signature, publication or external handoff.

composition.organization-settings.boundary: One section at a time, chosen from a list of links (a Select on a phone). Read-only and not-yet-built sections say so with a badge; no commercial, security or destructive control is offered.

composition.communications-manager.boundary: Letters are organization words sent through Missa. A batch is sent only after approval bound to its wording; a test send goes to the admin only; per-recipient results come from the durable mail ledger and are never inferred.

composition.edit-submission.boundary: A submitter changes Work titles, Work files and text or file answers only while the call is open, no reader is assigned and no decision exists, unless the organization locked the opportunity. Files must be the submitter's own Missa uploads; every change is recorded and shown in the organization's history.

composition.round-rubric.boundary: Each save creates an immutable rubric version; reads already scored keep their version. Readers score whole numbers per criterion in the reviewer score form, and the server computes the weighted 0 to 100 score used for ranking and calibration.

composition.submitter-questions.boundary: A submitter asks about their own submission from its receipt; the organization answers or closes it from Messages. Answers appear on the receipt and are emailed; who answered is never shown to the submitter.

composition.organization-customization.boundary: Accent choices are names for existing palette mappings in components/design-system/organization-palette.css; no raw colour is accepted or stored. Stage labels and transparency change wording and visibility only, never the recorded facts.

composition.submission-receipt.boundary: The submitter's own record of one hosted submission: where it stands, each Work with its own recorded decision, their answers, questions, history and payment. Withdrawal is confirmed in an AlertDialog. No reader, score or note is ever shown.

composition.submission-status-timeline.boundary: Submitter-facing journey derived from receipt, sent stage letters and recorded decisions under the organization's transparency setting. Never names readers, scores or notes.

composition.admin-publication-review.boundary: Platform-admin decision queue for review-agent holds. Approve publishes through the database publication gates; block suppresses. Hold reasons are plain text, not badges.

composition.application-tracker-preview.boundary: Device-local preview; no notification delivery or live calendar sync.

composition.application-preparation.boundary: Account-owned canonical applications and preparation; explicit recorded events, no submission on external navigation.

composition.creator-portfolio.embeddedBoundary: Embedded samples show identity and selected work only, keep the fictional sample label, and disable contact actions.

composition.creator-profile-addons.boundary: Visitor sections for the Editions, Shows and performances, Services, Teaching and Support add-ons. Enquiries open the profile's message form with a topic and a first line naming the item; there is no checkout and no price on Editions. Places left show only when stated. Support is one outbound link that says it leaves Missa and opens in a new tab. Embedded mode never shows them.
composition.creator-profile-addons.customRationale: Installed Item, Card and Table were inspected and not used for the rows: they fix a density and type scale that the profile's editorial rows (Newsreader titles, ruled lists, mono facts) do not share, and Badge is reachable only through the two semantic wrappers above. The rows follow the Track record and Upcoming grammar in public-profile.module.css.

composition.creator-profile-inbox.boundary: Senders never see the creator's address unless the creator replies by email; organizations are not told when an invitation is declined.

composition.creator-share-kit.boundary: Drawn only from the published profile: before the first publish it explains what is coming and offers Publish through the studio's own dialog; after changes it says the kit shows the last published version. Pictures come from /@handle/share.png and /@handle/story.png, event cards from /@handle/events/<id>. The signature (emails/creator-signature.ts) is text-only HTML with no stylesheet, image or tracking, and every field escaped. Copying uses the async Clipboard API, then a selection copy, then hands the text over to copy by hand.

composition.creator-event-card.boundary: One upcoming, published event with an id; unknown, past and unpublished events are the same 404 and the page is never indexed. The QR code (lib/qr-code.ts, inline SVG, error correction M, four-module quiet zone) always encodes the profile's https address. Print uses the browser's print dialog, which also saves a PDF; the page sets the A6 paper size in millimetres.

composition.creator-share-image.boundary: Generated PNGs. next/og cannot read CSS variables or the page's fonts, so colours come from the shared email constants (the Missa tokens as hex) and Newsreader, Instrument Sans and Fragment Mono are fetched as TTF, with the renderer's default face as the fallback. The story quotes the featured work only in the maker's own line breaks and never writes about the work.

composition.creator-work-page.typography: Newsreader for the title, standfirst and reading text; Fragment Mono for counts, years and part numbers only; Instrument Sans for everything else
composition.creator-work-page.boundary: Only a work the published profile shows has a page, so an unshown work or an unknown address is a 404 and an alias handle redirects. The page never carries decision ids; Confirmed is whatever the server derived for the track-record entry that names the work. A work with parts shows its parts; without parts it shows its own text, picture and audio.

composition.creator-work-page-fields.boundary: The page address is tidied as it is typed and the studio says in a sentence when the address a work gets is not the one asked for (reserved word, or an address another work has).

composition.writing-room.boundary: Rich text on printed pages the creator writes. Kept on the device until the account confirms it, and never overwritten by another device: refused text becomes a separate entry. No AI, suggestions, rewriting or analysis; only apps/web/lib/writing-repository.ts reads the text (enforced by lib/writing-boundary.test.ts). No WebMCP tools on /doc (or the old /write address, which redirects there).

composition.writing-library.boundary: Gathers, orders and opens pieces; never reads or changes their text. Projects, piece order, synopsis and status are kept only through apps/web/lib/writing-repository.ts (creator_writing_projects, migration 0097). Deleting a project keeps its pieces. Compile joins pieces in order for print, PDF or plain text in the browser.

input.writing-page.boundary: The printed pages a creator writes on in the writing room: rich text with every space and tab kept, each page with its own format. Long text inside a form stays input.long-text (Field + Textarea).

composition.auth-shell.boundary: Frame only: owns the main landmark, wordmark, legal links, and decorative photograph (hidden below 1024px and from assistive technology). Authentication, verification, and first-save logic stay in AuthForm. Form controls use Field, Input, InputOTP, Alert, Spinner, and Button; the Google action uses SocialAuthButton.

composition.creator-onboarding.boundary: Given and family names are supplied by the person and remain distinct from the normalized public handle. Country, city, timezone, career stage, travel willingness, and fee preference are private matching inputs. Country and time zone use searchable Combobox lists; time zones are validated on the server. Finish later saves the current choices and marks setup skipped; only a completed setup opens on the summary. The live match count and the welcome list read the public browse API: kinds of work widen the set (taxonomyMatch=any) while opportunity types, country eligibility, and the fee preference narrow it. They show open calls, never eligibility, and hide when the API is unavailable. When handle claiming is open, finishing waits for a confirmed available address.

composition.creator-workspace.boundary: Never infer an external application status or submission from a link open.

filter.creator-work-format.rules: Formats are built from what the work holds (Writing, Images, Sound, Film, Link), never from listed practices; a film's poster does not make it Images. Hidden when every work shares one format. Series joins only when two or more works share a series name and not every work is in one. A change is announced ('Showing 4 writing works.').

composition.creator-work-formats.boundary: Works that share a series group under a heading with a plate count. A wall label prints title, year, medium, size and edition, each only when the creator gave it. Pressing play on a film card opens the work with the film begun; opening the work any other way loads nothing from the film's host.

media.creator-film.boundary: The poster is the creator's own picture, so opening a page makes no request to YouTube or Vimeo. The frame is built only after a press, from the film id, on youtube-nocookie.com or player.vimeo.com (Vimeo with do-not-track on); the content-security-policy frame-src lists exactly those two origins (lib/video-embed-origins.ts). Any other link opens as an ordinary link in a new tab. A chapter reloads the frame at its start time; no provider script runs on Missa.

player.creator-audio.boundary: One recording at a time for the whole profile, kept playing while the visitor scrolls or closes a dialog. Nothing is fetched until someone presses play. Loading is also said in words; an error says what failed and Try again loads the file again; Close stops the recording. Chapters jump to a time and the current one is marked with aria-current.

feedback.creator-media-error.boundary: Says the image didn't load and the work is still here, and offers Try again. The work still opens; a failed picture never blocks its text, audio or film.

disclosure.creator-transcript.boundary: The words of a film or recording, opened on request with line breaks kept. Shown wherever the player is.

composition.submission-portal-studio.boundary: Relational, versioned Organization configuration. Save and lifecycle actions use optimistic concurrency; preview is explicitly an unsaved applicant projection.

composition.organization-structure-actio.boundary: Owners and Admins create Teams and Programs from Settings, under Structure. Rename, move, and archive stay withheld.

composition.organization-form-builder.boundary: Compatibility-workspace submission form inside the Opportunity editor. Field identity is preserved on save so applicant drafts stay matched; the relational workspace keeps using PortalStudio.

composition.organization-opportunity-lif.boundary: Publish and close are confirmed state transitions; closing uses the destructive variant and keeps received Submissions.

composition.organization-people-actions.boundary: Add, change role, and remove access. Server owner and last-admin safeguards decide every change; the invite response never reveals whether an email has a Missa account.

composition.organization-submission-acti.boundary: Assign one eligible member per round (duplicates refused client and server side), record one Work outcome per dialog with its consequence stated, and set up or complete a delivery task. Recording a decision never sends email.

composition.guide-article.boundary: Primitives keep their own variants; feature code passes them layout classes only (shadcn/no-restyle). Editorial type, density spacing (Spacious) and the cover palette live on plain elements. Guide cards use Card variant=interactive; open calls use the discovery collections' OpportunityBrowseProjectCard; callouts are default Alerts with a meaning icon; questions use the default Accordion; tables are ruled Tables that read as labelled records under a 36rem column.

composition.manuscript-match.boundary: Fit, odds, payoff and cost are deterministic scores from recorded facts, versioned with the decision model; the plan is guidance, not eligibility or a submission claim. Journal destinations remain source-linked and external.

action.account-menu.boundary: Authenticated account disclosure keeps its compact desktop footprint; the mobile trigger uses the 44px icon size.

action.accent-supporting.boundary: A supporting action may use Forest text and border without competing with the single filled primary action.

feedback.content-correction.boundary: Authenticated reports enter the support review queue; a report never changes public information automatically.

action.authentication.social.boundary: Rendered only for a configured provider; the OAuth callback provisions or links the existing Missa account before navigation.

composition.opportunities-browse.boundary: Shipped /opportunities catalogue using canonical public records and account-aware save actions. External navigation does not imply submission.

composition.opportunities-browse-preview.boundary: Design-review entry for the shared browse implementation; representative fixtures remain explicitly labelled and do not publish records.

composition.public-index-layout.boundary: Shared shipped layout contract for public directory and ranking indexes. The current implementation delegates to a legacy preview-named stylesheet without changing its visual behavior.

composition.magazine-index.boundary: Explicit seed preview; server-derived scores; no inferred submission or response.

composition.residency-index.boundary: Community reviews, funding badges, MRI scores, and multi-factor filtering.

composition.residency-comparison.boundary: Side-by-side residency comparison across funding, solitude, meals, and community feedback.

composition.discovery-journey-preview.boundary: Isolated local review route; signup is simulated; opportunity page reused unchanged; teal scoped to rankings preview.

composition.homepage-focused.boundary: Experimental review route. Navigation uses descriptive category links; live totals retain loading and retry states. HomepagePortfolio presents the canonical portfolio with installed Button theme choices; no account writes. Existing marketing tokens only. Footer painting shares one semantic footer with navigation and fades into its surface.

composition.homepage-hero.boundary: Shipped homepage hero. The semantic entry delegates to the reviewed legacy implementation; design-system routes continue to import the preview entry directly. One licensed documentary studio photograph is responsively cropped from a 3840px master and carries source, photographer and license metadata beside the asset; Forest remains an action accent rather than the dominant viewport field.

composition.homepage-studio.boundary: Finite user-requested 280ms panel phases; still equivalent; scene selection never saves preferences or submits work. Native responsive images, no generated video dependency.

composition.video-world.boundary: Experimental attributed reference study. Persistent video layers, user-requested forward/reverse clips, no live generation; not original Missa footage. Scoped 980ms controller choreography follows explicit cinematic direction.

composition.applications-design-preview.boundary: Isolated fictional design study; memory-only changes; no account writes, application destinations or reminder delivery.

composition.homepage-next-opening.boundary: Installed Embla with the wheel-gestures plugin for horizontal trackpad input, looping category navigation, pointer and keyboard controls. Card-05 image/content adaptation, four staggered live metrics, responsive container queries, reduced-motion equivalent and loading skeletons. Organizations uses the public directory profile total; counts have a plus suffix, never a fabricated value.

composition.goals-preview.boundary: Fictional local-state goals. No persistence, recommendation ranking or reminder delivery.

composition.goals-workspace.boundary: Account-owned persisted goals using canonical catalogue IDs and server scheduling

composition.homepage-continuation.boundary: Canonical OpportunityBrowseProjectCard with validated API records. Directory profile names, kinds, routes and logos from the backend; a credited official Headlands campus photograph provides the featured image. Image failures use the existing Avatar fallback. No fabricated opportunity or organization facts.

composition.cookie-consent.boundary: Site-wide analytics permission question. Decline leaves both the third-party analytics client and the first-party client event ledger unstarted. The choice is stored in localStorage with a cookie mirror and never gates product functionality.

composition.email-choice-prompt.boundary: One-time email question in the creator workspace for accounts created before reminder emails and the weekly digest were on by default. Shown only while notification_preferences.email_choice_at is null; accepting turns on email, reminders and the weekly digest, declining changes nothing, and either answer stops the question. On Free, which keeps reminders in the Inbox, the question and its confirmation are only about the weekly digest.

composition.homepage-workspace.boundary: Interactive public feature explorer with original fictional campaign photography. The homepage uses a one-work portfolio teaser; real public catalogue deadlines, local notification switches, and clearly labelled resettable sample submissions remain interactive. No private API write, delivery or publication. Existing app destinations retained. User-triggered motion with reduced-motion equivalent. Homepage preview starts with the White theme; five local theme choices remain interactive. Approved marketing-only forest, citron and sky surfaces use the scoped palette token chain.

composition.application-record.boundary: The one Tracker sheet for a tracked application, opened by /tracker?item=<id> or /tracker?application=<id>&section=<progress|prepare|timing|materials|notes|history> from every surface. Deadline, stages and plan come from deadline management; the record sections add progress with the lifecycle Saved, Preparing, Ready, Submitted, In review, Outcome, where each reached step shows its recorded date and provenance (recorded by you, Missa-hosted submission, received from the organization, inferred from source information) and never an invented date. External navigation never records a submission. One Forest action per region. No AI wording.

composition.creator-home.boundary: Derived entirely from Tracker state by lib/creator-home.ts. Names the week (busy, waiting, quiet, first run) in one generated sentence. This week's three ranks start-by passed or due, ready but unrecorded, closing this week, response check-ins, and Selected for you, one per application; the lead move carries the page's one Forest action. Home edits only through the record's own APIs: a lead preparation step is completed with PATCH /api/me/checklist-items/:id, and a due check-in is snoozed a week with PATCH /api/me/reminders/:id; every other row opens /tracker?application=<id>&section=<tab>. Goal pace compares an even spread from the goal's start with recorded submissions; preparing never counts as submitted. Replaces the former Your space at /workspace for creators.

composition.library-material.boundary: Owner-only material connections and immutable selected versions; editing reusable text changes future use.

composition.library-workspace.boundary: Private works, files and text; preserve existing editors and source file storage.

composition.application-reminders.boundary: User-created account-owned preparation, deadline and response reminders. The background worker delivers in-app only and observes opt-outs.

composition.creator-inbox.states: Briefing with consequence-first groups, first-use or caught-up empty state, structural loading, recoverable route error, read-state failure, reminders, email review and notification preferences.
composition.creator-inbox.responsive: Comfortable creator density; labelled row actions stack below content on narrow screens; the tab list scrolls without changing DOM order.
composition.creator-inbox.boundary: Actual account notifications, exact application links, snooze and read state. Empty and unavailable states never imply Tracker, application or provider state changed. Reuse existing email review.

composition.creator-following.boundary: Existing organizations and programs including closed rounds. Distinct organization and program disclosures; first-party verified calls drive notices.

composition.creator-recommendations.boundary: Actual account goals, preferences and Library work tags; contextual hide/restore, explicit match reasons, distinct current calls and between-round program planning. No eligibility or selection-probability claims.

composition.calendar-planning.boundary: Retains existing calendar grid and editor. Separate application dates, goal dates, personal time and reminder instants; owned application links and overlap feedback. Provider connection is not delivery confirmation.

UrgencyBadge.boundary: Time pressure only: ochre within seven days of a close, a calm neutral otherwise. Text is customer language such as 'Closes in 6 days'. Never pulses.

FeeBadge.boundary: An entry fee or 'No fee'. Renders nothing when the fee is unknown.

OrganizationMark.boundary: An organization's logo as a 48px contained mark (object-fit: contain on the card surface, radius-md), the treatment the directory already uses for organization icons. Shown on a card's plate only when the card has no official image; a logo never fills a cover. Decorative (alt="", aria-hidden) because the organization's name is always in the card text. Renders nothing if the logo fails to load.

MatchExplanationTrigger.boundary: Shows a percentage only when recorded evidence or watchouts exist; otherwise reads Limited data. The popover states its reasons, watchouts, and that fit is not eligibility.

ProcessBadge.boundary: Background process state (syncing, synced, waiting, not synced). A failed state is always paired with a recovery action.

PersonAvatar.boundary: A person's initials on one of twelve categorical hues derived from their identity, so a person keeps one colour on every surface. The colour identifies; it never states status.

LabelPill.boundary: A categorical label (criterion, category, opportunity) in one of twelve hues. Never used for status, which keeps its semantic badges.

DatePickerField.boundary: Chooses an ISO calendar date from a calendar popover in place of the browser's date input; optional Clear. The trigger is a field-style Button showing the formatted date or a placeholder.

SegmentedChoice.boundary: One visible choice from a short ordered set: a rubric score from 0 to the criterion's scale, a rubric's scale, or a Work decision. More than six options switch to the scale variant, which wraps to two rows of 44px targets below the small breakpoint and joins into one row above it. It is a radio group, so arrow keys move between options and each option has an accessible name; it never commits a destructive action on its own.

WorkDecisionBadge.boundary: Labels the recorded decision on one Work (Accepted, Waitlisted, Declined). It reflects a recorded decision only and never implies a letter was sent.

ListGroup.boundary: A collapsible section of a grouped Table variant="grid" list: a disclosure header row with a count, then its rows. Sections order a working list by what needs doing first; collapsing hides rows without filtering data.

DetailFields.boundary: Name and value rows at the top of a record's detail Sheet. Values are recorded facts; it holds no actions.

DeliveryPlanBadge.boundary: Labels where an accepted Work's delivery task stands (Needs setup, Active, Complete, or Overdue for a pending task past its due date). Complete means complete in Missa only.

ConfirmDialog.boundary: useConfirm() asks before removing, cancelling, closing or rotating something, in place of window.confirm. It resolves true only from the confirming button; Escape, Cancel and the backdrop resolve false. Destructive actions use the destructive button variant. The browser's confirm box is not used in product code.

DeliveryStateBadge.boundary: Labels a provider delivery record (Delivered, Accepted by provider, In progress, Needs attention). Accepted is never shown as delivered.

DecisionSummaryBadge.boundary: Labels the recorded decisions across a submission's Works (Not decided, Partly decided, Accepted, Mixed). It reflects recorded decisions only and never implies a letter was sent.

IntakeFlagBadge.boundary: Names an intake flag (Too many Works, Missing file, Repeat submitter) with its reason in the accessible name. A prompt to look; it never declines or hides a submission.

SettingsRow.boundary: One setting on a settings page: a heading and a sentence on what it does beside its controls, rows separated by a rule. Holds no save of its own; the form around it saves.

SettingsStateBadge.boundary: Marks a settings section that cannot be changed (Read only, Not available yet). Editable sections carry no badge.

HueTile.boundary: A small colour tile marking a record (a review round, a rubric criterion) with an icon or number on a categorical hue derived from the record's identity. A fixed place such as a navigation destination names its hue instead, so no two destinations collide. Tone soft (tinted tile, icon in the hue's ink) is the resting state; tone solid marks the current page in CreatorShell. Decorative and aria-hidden; the record's name always sits beside it.

CreatorShell.boundary: The signed-in account rail and its mobile drawer. Destinations are grouped (Find, Plan and track, Your work, Switch to) as Links styled with the Button nav variant, each with a HueTile in its own fixed hue; the current page lifts its tile from soft to solid and keeps aria-current. Collapsed, the rail shows tiles only and names each in a Tooltip. The account is a PersonAvatar opening a DropdownMenu (Profile, Plan, Log out).

CalibrationBadge.boundary: Labels a reader's scoring tendency (scores low, in line, scores high, too few scores) from the recorded calibration; the explanation sentence travels with it so the label never stands alone.

LetterStateBadge.boundary: Approval-gate state of an organization letter batch in customer language; sent is the only positive state and partly sent is a warning, never a success.

QuestionStateBadge.boundary: State of a question a submitter asked an organization: waiting for an answer, answered, or closed.

SubmissionStageBadge.boundary: Current step of a submitter's journey (received, in review, an announced stage, decision, withdrawn) derived from recorded events only.

PlanTierBadge.boundary: Labels a magazine's place in a submission plan from its recorded odds score: Long shot, Good fit or Likely. Guidance from recorded facts, never a prediction of acceptance.

FilterChip.boundary: Toggle choice announced with aria-pressed and shown with a check mark plus Forest outline; never a filled primary action.

ApplicationLabels.boundary: Opportunity type plus at most one personal status or availability label

ApplicationCalendarDelivery.boundary: Read-only delivery state for one application: private feed on/off, each provider connection (synced or reconnect), and planned sessions with Syncing…, Synced, Sync failed + Retry. Synced only after the provider queue reports success; the spinner shows only while a job is queued or running.

ApplicationEmailEvidence.boundary: Email forwarding or Gmail evidence only suggests a status. Nothing changes until the creator confirms; confirming records the event with source=email and closes the suggestion in one transaction. Shown only when an email integration is enabled.

SimilarOpportunities.boundary: Recovery after a decline, a withdrawal, or a missed deadline. Deterministic matches (lib/similar-opportunities.ts) from shared taxonomy, genres, kind of call, fee, and preparation time; each match lists its plain reasons. Never labelled AI or smart. Excludes tracked calls, the anchor, calls closing within 7 days, and calls hidden for this application; at most two per organization. Save to Tracker or Not for me.

PreSubmitCheck.boundary: Before you submit: required materials, word limit against saved text, page limit, anonymous-review name check across titles, file names, and saved text, and file types. Each row is Passed, Needs attention, or Check manually with the status written beside its icon; anything Missa cannot read (file contents, page counts, document properties, unrecorded file types) is Check manually, never Passed.

EditorialMotif.boundary: Decorative cover motif (orbit, burst, steps, frame) in currentColor for discovery collection and guide covers. Always inside an aria-hidden cover.

GuideTypography.boundary: Class recipes for long-form guide text on plain elements: display and section headings in Newsreader, body large and lists in Instrument Sans, inline code and dates in Fragment Mono, Forest links. Never applied to components/ui primitives.

GuideChecklist.boundary: A checklist inside a guide article. Ticks stay in this browser and Copy list puts the items on the clipboard. Not an application record.

GuideToc.boundary: On this page for a guide: a sticky rail marking the current section with aria-current=location on wide screens, a closed Collapsible with an outline Button trigger on narrow ones.

GoalSubmissionProgress.boundary: One circle per submission up to 24; numeric progressbar for larger targets. Preparation does not increment progress.

ApplicationStateBadge.boundary: A creator's personal application state (Check-in due, On track, 1 day behind, Ready to record, Not selected). The label states the meaning; declined and withdrawn stay neutral.

ApplicationRunway.boundary: Time left against Missa's start-by estimate: Ochre slipped days or Lichen slack, then the Forest work window, with today marked and every part stated in text. Custom because Progress shows one value and the runway needs two segments plus a marker; inspected Progress, CircularProgress, Slider, and Studio progress families first.

EmailChoicePrompt.boundary: Non-urgent permission question rendered above workspace content, not modal. The installed Alert is not used because it hard-codes role=alert; only the save failure uses role=alert.

PlanProduct.boundary: The creator's plan page: current plan and Free allowance, the Plus offer with prices read from Stripe, and one action (upgrade, or manage in Stripe). Status messages use role=status; only a failed checkout or portal request uses role=alert.

TextRemindersSettings.boundary: Plus-only text (SMS) reminder settings, in notification preferences and inline in ReminderChannels: Free creators see what Plus adds and a link to /plan; Plus creators add a number with PhoneInput (opened on the country of the browser language, checked with isValidPhoneNumber before a code is sent), confirm it with a six-digit InputOTP code, then use one Switch to turn texts on or off, change or remove the number. Every change saves immediately through /api/me/sms; the plan is plain text, not a Badge. Always states 'Reply STOP to end. Msg & data rates may apply.' Status uses role=status; only failures use role=alert.

ReminderChannels.boundary: Where this creator's reminders go, shown where a reminder is set (Tracker item Reminders) and on the last onboarding screen. Free sees the Inbox and an UpgradeHint for email and text, and is never asked for a phone number, so no verification text is sent for a plan that cannot receive one. Plus and Pro see every channel that is on and a Button that opens TextRemindersSettings in place (aria-expanded, aria-controls). Until /api/me/notification-preferences answers, it says only what is true for every plan. Composition over Button because the installed Collapsible adds a second trigger pattern for a single inline form.

CookieConsent.boundary: Permission question for optional analytics. Non-modal region above the page, one decision per visitor, no analytics client or first-party event ledger runs before an explicit Accept. The installed Alert is not used because it hard-codes role=alert.

ProvenanceBadge.rule: Confirmed only when the server matched a Missa acceptance; the popover always explains the source in plain language.

CollaborationBadge.rule: Confirmed only when the other creator's published profile credits this creator back, which the server reads on every request. Awaiting is shown to the owner in the studio and never to a visitor. Both states are written out; the dashed outline never carries the meaning alone.
CollaborationBadge.boundary: Not a ProvenanceBadge state: that mark means an organization recorded an outcome on Missa and has three states for the source of a record entry. A credit between two creators has a different rule and an owner-only state, so it is its own semantic component on the same Popover pattern and badge styles.

AvailabilityChip.rule: A 'from' entry whose date has passed reads as open; meaning never depends on colour alone.

EditionAvailability.rule: Shown only when the edition size and the number left are both stated and agree: '4 of 12 available', or 'Sold out' at none. The label carries the meaning; the dot and tone only help the eye. No price, no checkout.

ShowKindTag.rule: A tiny read-only tag for the kind of show; a show of kind 'other' has no tag.

DateConfidenceBadge.boundary: Whether a date is confirmed by the organization's source, predicted by Missa from past cycles (dotted underline, never presented as the organization's), changed since first recorded, or needs checking. The title carries the plain-language explanation.

UpgradeHint.boundary: One calm line naming what a plan adds and a link to /plan. Says what the creator gets, never what they lose; no alarm colour, no modal.

WritingSnapshots.boundary: Snapshots of the open piece: take one under an optional name, compare it line by line with the text now (struck-through and marked lines with screen-reader prefixes), restore it after keeping the current text as a snapshot, or delete it. Read and written only through apps/web/lib/writing-repository.ts (creator_writing_snapshots, migration 0098).

WritingCall.boundary: Ties the open piece to a call in the creator's tracker (call_id on creator_writing_entries, migration 0099, kept only through apps/web/lib/writing-repository.ts). Shows the call, its links and the creator's checklist, and runs the word, page, materials and anonymous-review checks of lib/writing-call.ts in the browser on the piece's own text; the text is never sent for them. Reuses PreSubmitCheckList for the checks. The footer shows words against the call's limit.

WritingPlanner.boundary: A project's planner, part of Plus (creatorFeatures().writingPlanner): Tabs for a corkboard of index cards (Item, in binder order or in lanes by plotline, status or point of view) and an outline Table with words against targets and a TableFooter total. Cards are edited in a Dialog of Field, Input, Textarea, NativeSelect and Checkbox; plotlines in a Dialog with HueTile markers. Cards hold the writer's notes, never the text (lib/writing-cards.ts, migration 0100). Free accounts keep WritingOutline with one UpgradeHint.

WritingWordCount.boundary: Counts for the open piece in a Dialog of DetailFields: pages, words, characters with and without spaces, reading time. With a selection, each count reads 'n of total'. Opens from the footer count, More, or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+C. Counting is arithmetic on the text in the browser; nothing reads its meaning.

WritingFind.boundary: A search landmark under the header that finds and replaces across every page and canvas text box in reading order, marking matches with warning tokens. Ctrl/Cmd+F or H opens it; Enter, Shift+Enter and Escape move and close.

WritingLibrary.boundary: The writing room's library: projects, a binder of each project's pieces (drag by the handle with the installed Sortable, or Move up and Move down in each piece's menu for keyboard and screen readers), loose pieces, the outline of synopses and statuses, and the compile options. Built from installed primitives only.

WritingPages.boundary: Printed pages (A4, US Letter, A5, chapbook) drawn at paper size, or a paperless draft view on small screens. Text flows from page to page as it is written; pages the writer adds stay apart. Any page can be a free canvas (components/missa/writing-canvas.tsx) of text boxes placed in millimetres, moved by a drag handle or by arrow keys on the focused handle, and printed exactly. Each page is a Tiptap (ProseMirror, MIT core only; no Tiptap AI or cloud packages) editor with its own alignment, line and letter spacing, margins, typeface and size; spaces, tabs and line breaks are kept as typed. Tab writes a tab (in a list it nests the item); Escape then Tab leaves the page. Ctrl or Cmd + Enter is a page break and More offers a section break, as in Google Docs and Word: a page break keeps the section's format, a section break starts its own; a muted, unprinted label between pages names each break, and Backspace at a page's start removes a page break. Optional focus dimming (lib/writing-focus.ts) gives everything but the paragraph or sentence in hand the muted-foreground token (AA in light and dark, never printed); typewriter scrolling is instant, never animated. The caret marks focus. Gap recorded: Textarea and the 20 local Studio textarea variants are plain-text form fields; none offers rich text, pages or per-page format, so this is the documented editor exception to 'Contenteditable without editor requirements'.
